checks: Checked the locator in original note 5ef2792a4d153635, §§1–6, (1)–(15). The result preserves the positive-limit hypotheses and uses no claim from the later lower-rank or example sections.

Orthogonally rotating the image of the last-coordinate subspace onto itself gives the required block lower-triangular map, with both diagonal blocks invertible and unchanged determinant magnitude and diameters. The componentwise linear parts preserve the anchored inclusions and the accepted representation-preserving centering gives the original affine recovery map.

For two round normalizations of the same anchor, width in direction v of its second image is the width in direction S-transpose v of its first image. An inball gives the lower bound and an enclosing ball gives the upper bound, proving the two stated operator norm bounds. Projection to the first block gives the induced fine bounds, and applying each to a nearest lattice point proves both covering-radius inequalities, regardless of centering offsets.

In the original sample at u, the residual base is A u minus the fine component of the centering. For every measurable subtrace of that section, residual covolume times residual volume multiplies the original value by |det A det C|=1/M. Translations do not change the radius or covolume; an isometric placement adds no Jacobian. In s=0, the last determinant is one and the section mass counts the sampled point.

Apply the accepted box estimate separately to every site and its actual coset, with Voronoi cell contained in the cube of its covering radius. Empty and lower-dimensional traces are covered by the estimate; the whole trace gives the total mass bound. The normalized error follows from the triangle inequality with denominator at least 1 minus the summed error, which tends to zero over finitely many sites.

Interior approximation is in one fixed positive limiting fiber, so the accepted within-fiber continuity applies. Hausdorff convergence contains a smaller concentric ball in the late fibers by support functions. Rounding only the first block within the actual coset preserves feasibility in both the late and limiting fibers. The limiting coarse laws converge in total variation on their fixed planes by dominated convergence of the indicators, then uniform cap error transfers the same-point depth to the normalized weighted fine law.

Every original closed halfspace containing the recovered point pulls back to a containing closed halfspace or to the whole lift. Its normalized mass agrees under the exact pushforward, so the infimum on the original side cannot be smaller. Eventually positive fine mass gives a maximum on the compact finite union of sampled fibers by upper semicontinuity of closed-halfspace depth.

For a retained point, every full cap contains at least the retained raw mass. Thus the normalized factor is T_+/T, including limit zero; a bounded omitted fine mass relative to retained coarse mass gives the reciprocal factor in the proof. No implication from zero omitted coarse mass to zero omitted fine mass is used.

Independently checked a distinguishing scale: for one fiber [0,1] × [0,h²] at grid h Z and h=1/j, the determinant-1/M block map diag(1,h^-2) gives a fixed square and normalized radius h/2, whereas the original radius divided by M=h² diverges.

dependencies.hypotheses_mapping: Finite lattice-complete spanning P, compatible full m-bodies, and positive limiting mass ratios are exactly its lift hypotheses. Its proof allows orthogonal postcomposition before centering and yields the required fixed planes, affine recovery, compact subsequences, and within-fiber continuity.

Its convex-set estimate in the proof applies site by site to the residual bodies and their closed halfspace traces; the containing box and Voronoi-cell cube give its R and delta. No common cross-component lattice is assumed.

overlap.comparison: Its fine recovery assumes a bounded original placement and an original mesh that is little-o of original coarse mass, and its numerical depth conclusion uses lower-rank sharp bounds. It does not cover the transformed mesh example above or compare each actual weighted normalized coset directly to a limiting lift.
Provides the underlying compact coarse lift, affine recovery and within-fiber continuity. It does not require preservation of the fine subspace or compare a sampled measure after normalization.
Provides the bounded convex-set quadrature estimate; neither the changing component normalizations nor feasible fine-point recovery is part of that lemma.
The retained raw-mass monotonicity is the same elementary mechanism, there for coarse fiber volume. Here the mass factor is the actual fine mass fraction, which need not track the coarse fraction.

readability: The lift map in the pushforward assertion is the affine recovery map from the lifted placement to the original placement. The retained clause is conditional on applying the recovery hypotheses to the retained family; it does not assume that discarded coarse-negligible sites are fine-negligible.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The block-preserving full-shape construction and exact weighted pushforward give fine mass convergence and recover depth at actual original fine points on each convergent lift subsequence.
